reason: The exposed core should cool by radiating energy into space.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making carbon and then mixing it into the envelope made the wind’s enrichment understandable, rather than just presenting the wind as a finished product.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial shell-fusion combination was fairly predictable, though it established the giant’s structure.

surprise.text: Pulsation exposed the hot core before the carbon-bearing wind sequence was complete; I had expected it mainly to loosen the outer layers.

arbitrary.text: The attempted mixing at step 3 was premature, but the compatibility feedback made the missing helium-burning step clear; it did not feel arbitrary afterward.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how material from the different stellar paths enters the mixed cloud, especially after the useful contrast between a wind and a supernova.
